jamal: FYI ran into a weird parity bug between node/python SDKs around request-id + retries + OTEL. logs show different req ids for retry attempts, and our scrubber only matched the original id so some retry logs slipped unredacted.
maria: ouch. which SDK exhibited the different behaviour?
jamal: python sdk. it generates a new `x-redwood-reqid` on each retry attempt in the HTTP transport. node keeps the same req on retry. example: `curl -H "x-redwood-reqid: r1" ...` then retry emits `r2`. our logging scrub rule only looks for `req=` that matches span.attributes['request.id'] (set at send time) so the mismatch bypassed it.
anya: so traces link to original span but logs have different ids? that will make debugging impossible. any repro?
jamal: small repro in `sampleapps/credit-check` - trigger an auth-failure that causes 401->refresh->retry. logs: ```2026-03-01T10:02:01Z DEBUG req=r1 auth=refresh start
2026-03-01T10:02:02Z DEBUG req=r2 auth=retry success user_email=alice@example.com``` second line leaked email because scrub looked up r1.
ryan: that explains the leak. scrub needs to be tolerant of retry-generated ids or we should not rotate req ids across retries.
maria: agreed. two choices: (A) change python transport to preserve initial req id across retry attempts, or (B) change scrubber to check current span context/parent for alternate ids and sanitize by key names instead of exact req match.
sec-jen: from security POV (and GDPR) easiest is to never allow PII in any debug-level logs regardless of id parity. prefer a defense-in-depth: (1) preserve req id, (2) expand scrub matching, (3) add global env REDACT_EXTRA_KEYS that forces scrub of common PII keys (`user_email`, `email`, `phone`).
jamal: i prototyped a minimal change: python transport now `preserve_reqid=True` by default and sets header `x-redwood-retained-reqid` so downstream telemetry can see original. also expanded scrub logic to check `user_email` keys in record meta.
anya: nice. how about OTEL span correlation? does python SDK attach request.id to span attributes like node does?
jamal: python was only adding `http.request_id` to the span on initial send. i updated it to set span.set_attribute('redwood.request_id', original_reqid) on each retry start so the scrubber can look up trace->request id mapping more reliably.
ryan: can we add a unit test that simulates N retries and asserts no `@` or `.com` in captured debug output, and an integration job that runs the auth refresh flow in the sampleapp?
maria: yes. i'll add tests and a lint rule that flags any logger calls including common PII keys at DEBUG level in our SDKs.
sec-jen: also add an assertion in CI smoke: `integration/sampleapp/no-pii-in-logs` that runs the signup/credit flow with retries enabled. If it fails, block the canary.
ci-bot: opened CI run 4120 for branch `fix/python-reqid-retry`  https://ci.redwood/4120 (failing on flake but scrub assertions present).
jamal: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/256  preserves reqid + adds span attr + expands scrub matching. requesting @maria and @ryan review.
ryan: quick look: small nit on naming `x-redwood-retained-reqid` vs reusing `x-redwood-reqid` header; i'd prefer to reuse same header and not proliferate names. also please add doc string explaining why preserve default is on.
maria: i'll do cross-sdk parity check: node, python, go. node already preserves id; go needs check. i'll open follow-up for go if needed.
ci-bot: integration test `integration/sampleapp/no-pii-in-logs` added and failing on `main`. feature branch shows passing locally.
anya: plan for rollout?
jamal: merge to canary after approvals, run canary for 24h with CI smoke gating. if green, promote to prod and set REDACT_EXTRA_KEYS env var in prod and staging to include `user_email,email`.
sec-jen: ensure release notes call out request-id behavior change and the added env variable. also mention the scrub expansion so security teams can audit.
maria: merged to canary. kicking canary deploy and enabling CI smoke for parity tests across languages.
ci-bot: canary deploy started: canary/2026-03-02-08:15  monitoring scrub assertions.
anya: thanks all. follow-up items: (1) docs: SDK retry semantics section, (2) onboard sampleapp README: reproduce steps to test no-PII, (3) add a short explainer in dev onboarding about stubbed retries causing surprising logs. :memo:
sec-jen: closing note: prefer preserving req id across retries as default platform behavior. gives consistent telemetry and simpler scrub rules. good catch folks. :shield:
